       2667 +  ## 7. Twitch/Discord Platform Integration (TwitchIO, discord.py)
       2668 +  
       2669 +  ### Overview
       2670 +  Integrate the AI companion with Twitch chat and Discord servers using 
            + TwitchIO and discord.py, allowing the character to interact with live stream
            +  viewers, respond to chat messages, and participate in Discord communities. 
            + This replicates Neuro-sama's streaming setup.
       2671 +  
       2672 +  ### What It Is and What It Does
       2673 +  Platform integration connects the AI to external communication platforms:
       2674 +  
       2675 +  **Twitch Integration:**
       2676 +  - Read chat messages in real-time
       2677 +  - Respond to viewers by username
       2678 +  - React to channel events (raids, subscriptions, bits)
       2679 +  - Participate in polls, predictions
       2680 +  - Moderate chat (timeouts, bans via commands)
       2681 +  - Track viewer sentiment and engagement
       2682 +  
       2683 +  **Discord Integration:**
       2684 +  - Join voice/text channels
       2685 +  - Respond to mentions and messages
       2686 +  - Run slash commands (`/ask`, `/chat`, `/image`)
       2687 +  - Voice chat support (combine with VAD + TTS)
       2688 +  - Role management, moderation
       2689 +  - Server statistics and analytics
       2690 +  
       2691 +  This transforms the AI from local companion to public personality, 
            + enabling:
       2692 +  - **Live streaming:** AI co-hosts streams, reacts to gameplay
       2693 +  - **Community building:** 24/7 Discord presence
       2694 +  - **Viewer interaction:** Personalized responses to thousands of users
       2695 +  - **Content creation:** Clip-worthy moments from AI interactions
       2696 +  
       2697 +  ### Code Example
       2698 +  
       2699 +  ```python
       2700 +  # backend/integrations/twitch_bot.py
       2701 +  from twitchio.ext import commands
       2702 +  from typing import Optional
       2703 +  import asyncio
       2704 +  import logging
       2705 +  from backend.llm.registry import get_llm_adapter
       2706 +  from backend.tts.registry import get_tts_adapter
       2707 +  
       2708 +  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
       2709 +  
       2710 +  class WaifuTwitchBot(commands.Bot):
       2711 +      """
       2712 +      Twitch bot integration for AI companion.
       2713 +  
       2714 +      Connects to Twitch chat, responds to messages using LLM,
       2715 +      and can speak responses via TTS (for stream overlay).
       2716 +      """
       2717 +  
       2718 +      def __init__(
       2719 +          self,
       2720 +          access_token: str,
       2721 +          prefix: str = "!",
       2722 +          initial_channels: list = None,
       2723 +          character_id: int = 1
       2724 +      ):
       2725 +          """
       2726 +          Initialize Twitch bot.
       2727 +  
       2728 +          Args:
       2729 +              access_token: Twitch OAuth token
       2730 +              prefix: Command prefix (default: "!")
       2731 +              initial_channels: List of channels to join
       2732 +              character_id: Which character to use for responses
       2733 +          """
       2734 +          super().__init__(
       2735 +              token=access_token,
       2736 +              prefix=prefix,
       2737 +              initial_channels=initial_channels or []
       2738 +          )
       2739 +          self.character_id = character_id
       2740 +          self.llm = None
       2741 +          self.tts = None
       2742 +          self.response_queue = asyncio.Queue()
       2743 +  
       2744 +          logger.info(f"Twitch bot initialized for channels: 
            + {initial_channels}")
       2745 +  
       2746 +      async def event_ready(self):
       2747 +          """Called when bot connects to Twitch."""
       2748 +          logger.info(f"✅ Twitch bot ready | User: {self.nick}")
       2749 +          logger.info(f"Connected to channels: {[c.name for c in 
            + self.connected_channels]}")
       2750 +  
       2751 +          # Initialize LLM and TTS
       2752 +          from backend.server import get_llm, get_tts
       2753 +          self.llm = get_llm()
       2754 +          self.tts = get_tts()
       2755 +  
       2756 +      async def event_message(self, message):
       2757 +          """
       2758 +          Called when a message is received in chat.
       2759 +  
       2760 +          Args:
       2761 +              message: TwitchIO Message object
       2762 +          """
       2763 +          # Ignore messages from the bot itself
       2764 +          if message.echo:
       2765 +              return
       2766 +  
       2767 +          # Handle commands first
       2768 +          await self.handle_commands(message)
       2769 +  
       2770 +          # Check if message mentions bot or is directed at bot
       2771 +          if self.should_respond(message):
       2772 +              await self.generate_response(message)
       2773 +  
       2774 +      def should_respond(self, message) -> bool:
       2775 +          """
       2776 +          Determine if bot should respond to this message.
       2777 +  
       2778 +          Args:
       2779 +              message: TwitchIO Message object
       2780 +  
       2781 +          Returns:
       2782 +              True if bot should respond
       2783 +          """
       2784 +          content = message.content.lower()
       2785 +  
       2786 +          # Respond if mentioned by name
       2787 +          if self.nick.lower() in content:
       2788 +              return True
       2789 +  
       2790 +          # Respond to specific keywords
       2791 +          keywords = ["waifu", "ai", "hello bot"]
       2792 +          if any(kw in content for kw in keywords):
       2793 +              return True
       2794 +  
       2795 +          # Random chance to respond (5%)
       2796 +          import random
       2797 +          if random.random() < 0.05:
       2798 +              return True
       2799 +  
       2800 +          return False
       2801 +  
       2802 +      async def generate_response(self, message):
       2803 +          """
       2804 +          Generate and send AI response to chat message.
       2805 +  
       2806 +          Args:
       2807 +              message: TwitchIO Message object
       2808 +          """
       2809 +          try:
       2810 +              logger.info(f"Generating response to: {message.author.name}: 
            + {message.content}")
       2811 +  
       2812 +              # Build context
       2813 +              prompt = f"Viewer {message.author.name} said: 
            + {message.content}\n\nRespond naturally in Twitch chat (keep it short, under 
            + 400 chars)."
       2814 +  
       2815 +              # Get character system prompt
       2816 +              # (Would load from database in real implementation)
       2817 +              system_prompt = "You are a friendly AI VTuber streaming on 
            + Twitch. Be entertaining, witty, and engage with chat."
       2818 +  
       2819 +              messages = [
       2820 +                  {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
       2821 +                  {"role": "user", "content": prompt}
       2822 +              ]
       2823 +  
       2824 +              # Get LLM response
       2825 +              response = await self.llm.chat(
       2826 +                  messages=messages,
       2827 +                  model="local-model",
       2828 +                  max_tokens=100  # Keep responses short for chat
       2829 +              )
       2830 +  
       2831 +              # Clean response (remove newlines, truncate if too long)
       2832 +              response = response.replace("\n", " ").strip()
       2833 +              if len(response) > 400:
       2834 +                  response = response[:397] + "..."
       2835 +  
       2836 +              # Send to chat
       2837 +              await message.channel.send(f"@{message.author.name} 
            + {response}")
       2838 +  
       2839 +              logger.info(f"Sent response: {response}")
       2840 +  
       2841 +          except Exception as e:
       2842 +              logger.error(f"Error generating response: {e}")
       2843 +  
       2844 +      @commands.command(name="ask")
       2845 +      async def ask_command(self, ctx: commands.Context, *, question: str):
       2846 +          """
       2847 +          !ask <question> - Ask the AI a question.
       2848 +  
       2849 +          Args:
       2850 +              ctx: Command context
       2851 +              question: User's question
       2852 +          """
       2853 +          await ctx.send(f"@{ctx.author.name} Thinking...")
       2854 +  
       2855 +          try:
       2856 +              # Generate response
       2857 +              messages = [
       2858 +                  {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful AI 
            + assistant on Twitch. Answer questions concisely."},
       2859 +                  {"role": "user", "content": question}
       2860 +              ]
       2861 +  
       2862 +              response = await self.llm.chat(messages=messages, 
            + max_tokens=150)
       2863 +              response = response.replace("\n", " ").strip()[:400]
       2864 +  
       2865 +              await ctx.send(f"@{ctx.author.name} {response}")
       2866 +  
       2867 +          except Exception as e:
       2868 +              await ctx.send(f"@{ctx.author.name} Oops, something went 
            + wrong!")
       2869 +              logger.error(f"!ask command error: {e}")
       2870 +  
       2871 +      @commands.command(name="stats")

       2880 +          """
       2881 +          !voice <text> - Generate TTS audio for stream overlay.
       2882 +  
       2883 +          Args:
       2884 +              ctx: Command context
       2885 +              text: Text to speak
       2886 +          """
       2887 +          try:
       2888 +              # Generate TTS
       2889 +              tts_result = await self.tts.synthesize(
       2890 +                  text=text,
       2891 +                  voice_id="default"
       2892 +              )
       2893 +  
       2894 +              # Notify chat
       2895 +              await ctx.send(f"🔊 Speaking: \"{text}\"")
       2896 +  
       2897 +              # Add to response queue (stream overlay would poll this)
       2898 +              await self.response_queue.put({
       2899 +                  "type": "tts",
       2900 +                  "text": text,
       2901 +                  "audio_url": tts_result["audio_url"],
       2902 +                  "user": ctx.author.name
       2903 +              })
       2904 +  
       2905 +          except Exception as e:
       2906 +              await ctx.send("Sorry, voice synthesis failed!")
       2907 +              logger.error(f"!voice error: {e}")

       2909 +      async def get_tts_queue(self):
       2910 +          """
       2911 +          Get next TTS response from queue.
       2912 +  
       2913 +          Stream overlay can poll this endpoint to play audio.
       2914 +  
       2915 +          Returns:
       2916 +              TTS response dict or None
       2917 +          """
       2918 +          if not self.response_queue.empty():
       2919 +              return await self.response_queue.get()
       2920 +          return None

       3205 +  ### Alternatives Considered
       3206 +  
       3207 +  **1. YouTube Live Chat Integration**
       3208 +  - **Approach:** Use `pytchat` library to read YouTube live chat
       3209 +  - **Why Not:** Smaller audience than Twitch for VTubers
       3210 +  - **Use Case:** If streaming to YouTube
       3211 +  
       3212 +  **2. Kick.com Integration**
       3213 +  - **Approach:** Use Kick chat API (unofficial)
       3214 +  - **Why Not:** No official API, smaller platform
       3215 +  - **Use Case:** If platform grows
       3216 +  
       3217 +  **3. Matrix/Element Integration (Decentralized)**
       3218 +  - **Approach:** Connect to Matrix protocol servers
       3219 +  - **Why Not:** Niche platform, less VTuber presence
       3220 +  - **Use Case:** If privacy-focused community
       3221 +  
       3222 +  **4. Telegram Bot**
       3223 +  - **Approach:** Use python-telegram-bot library
       3224 +  - **Why Not:** Different use case (messaging vs streaming chat)
       3225 +  - **Use Case:** For direct user interactions
       3226 +  
       3227 +  **5. No Platform Integration (Local Only)**
       3228 +  - **Approach:** Keep AI companion purely local
       3229 +  - **Why Not:** Limits use cases, no streaming/community features
       3230 +  - **Use Case:** Privacy-focused users who don't stream
       3231 +

            + content creation and community building, not just local use.
       3235 +

       3237 +  - **VTuber Hub:** Largest VTuber streaming platform
       3238 +  - **Real-Time:** Chat moves fast, AI can respond instantly
       3239 +  - **Monetization:** Bits, subs, ads support creators
       3240 +  - **Clips:** Easy to create viral moments
       3241 +  
       3242 +  **Why Discord:**
       3243 +  - **Community:** Most VTubers have Discord servers (10k-100k members)
       3244 +  - **Persistent:** 24/7 presence, not just during streams
       3245 +  - **Rich Features:** Voice, slash commands, roles, bots
       3246 +  - **Engagement:** Fans hang out between streams
       3247 +  
       3248 +  **Why Not YouTube Live:**
       3249 +  - Still important, but Twitch dominates VTuber space
       3250 +  - Can add later with same architecture
       3251 +  
       3252 +  **Content Moderation Strategy:**
       3253 +  - Use sentiment analysis to detect toxic input
       3254 +  - Blacklist inappropriate topics in system prompt
       3255 +  - Rate-limit responses to prevent spam

       3269 +  ## 8. Game Integration Framework - Minecraft AI (mineflayer, Baritone)
       3270 +  
       3271 +  ### Overview
       3272 +  Implement a game integration framework starting with Minecraft, allowing 
            + the AI companion to play games, respond to in-game events, and interact with
            +  the user while gaming. This uses mineflayer (JavaScript Minecraft bot) and 
            + Baritone (pathfinding) to enable autonomous gameplay.
       3273 +  
       3274 +  ### What It Is and What It Does
       3275 +  Game integration connects the AI to games, enabling:
       3276 +  
       3277 +  **Minecraft Integration:**
       3278 +  - Join Minecraft servers as a bot player
       3279 +  - Navigate the world (walk, jump, mine, build)
       3280 +  - Respond to chat messages from players
       3281 +  - Complete tasks ("go to coordinates", "mine diamonds", "build house")
       3282 +  - React to game events (damage, death, player interactions)
       3283 +  - Autonomous gameplay with Baritone pathfinding
       3284 +  
       3285 +  **Framework Capabilities:**
       3286 +  - **Adapter Pattern:** Plugins for different games (Minecraft, Roblox, 
            + etc.)
       3287 +  - **Event System:** Subscribe to game events (player_join, chat_message, 
            + damage)
       3288 +  - **Action API:** Unified interface for game actions (move, interact, 
            + speak)
       3289 +  - **State Tracking:** Maintain game state (inventory, position, health)
       3290 +  - **LLM Integration:** AI decides actions based on game context
       3291 +  
       3292 +  Example interactions:
       3293 +  - User: "Let's play Minecraft together!"
       3294 +  - AI: *joins server* "I'm online! Where should I meet you?"
       3295 +  - User: "Come to spawn and help me mine"
       3296 +  - AI: *navigates to spawn, mines nearby* "Found some iron ore!"
       3297 +  
       3298 +  This replicates how Neuro-sama plays games with Vedal (Minecraft, OSU!, 
            + etc.).
       3299 +  
       3300 +  ### Code Example
       3301 +  
       3302 +  ```python
       3303 +  # backend/games/game_base.py
       3304 +  from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
       3305 +  from typing import Dict, Any, Callable
       3306 +  import logging
       3307 +  
       3308 +  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
       3309 +  
       3310 +  class GameAdapter(ABC):
       3311 +      """
       3312 +      Base class for game integration adapters.
       3313 +  
       3314 +      Each game (Minecraft, Roblox, etc.) implements this interface.
       3315 +      """
       3316 +  
       3317 +      def __init__(self):
       3318 +          """Initialize game adapter."""
       3319 +          self.connected = False
       3320 +          self.event_handlers = {}
       3321 +  
       3322 +      @abstractmethod
       3323 +      async def connect(self, **kwargs):
       3324 +          """
       3325 +          Connect to game server.
       3326 +  
       3327 +          Args:
       3328 +              **kwargs: Game-specific connection params (host, port, 
            + username, etc.)
       3329 +          """
       3330 +          pass
       3331 +  
       3332 +      @abstractmethod
       3333 +      async def disconnect(self):
       3334 +          """Disconnect from game server."""
       3335 +          pass
       3336 +  
       3337 +      @abstractmethod
       3338 +      async def send_chat(self, message: str):
       3339 +          """
       3340 +          Send chat message in game.
       3341 +  
       3342 +          Args:
       3343 +              message: Chat message to send
       3344 +          """
       3345 +          pass
       3346 +  
       3347 +      @abstractmethod
       3348 +      async def get_state(self) -> Dict:
       3349 +          """
       3350 +          Get current game state.
       3351 +  
       3352 +          Returns:
       3353 +              dict: Game state (position, health, inventory, etc.)
       3354 +          """
       3355 +          pass
       3356 +  
       3357 +      @abstractmethod
       3358 +      async def execute_action(self, action: str, params: Dict = None):
       3359 +          """
       3360 +          Execute a game action.
       3361 +  
       3362 +          Args:
       3363 +              action: Action name (e.g., "move", "mine", "place_block")
       3364 +              params: Action parameters
       3365 +          """
       3366 +          pass
       3367 +  
       3368 +      def on(self, event: str, handler: Callable):
       3369 +          """
       3370 +          Register event handler.
       3371 +  
       3372 +          Args:
       3373 +              event: Event name (e.g., "chat", "damage", "player_join")
       3374 +              handler: Async callback function
       3375 +          """
       3376 +          if event not in self.event_handlers:
       3377 +              self.event_handlers[event] = []
       3378 +          self.event_handlers[event].append(handler)
       3379 +  
       3380 +      async def emit(self, event: str, data: Any):
       3381 +          """
       3382 +          Emit event to registered handlers.
       3383 +  
       3384 +          Args:
       3385 +              event: Event name
       3386 +              data: Event data
       3387 +          """
       3388 +          if event in self.event_handlers:
       3389 +              for handler in self.event_handlers[event]:
       3390 +                  try:
       3391 +                      await handler(data)
       3392 +                  except Exception as e:
       3393 +                      logger.error(f"Event handler error ({event}): {e}")
       3394 +  
       3395 +  
       3396 +  # backend/games/minecraft_adapter.py
       3397 +  from backend.games.game_base import GameAdapter
       3398 +  import asyncio
       3399 +  import json
       3400 +  import subprocess
       3401 +  import logging
       3402 +  
       3403 +  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
       3404 +  
       3405 +  class MinecraftAdapter(GameAdapter):
       3406 +      """
       3407 +      Minecraft game adapter using mineflayer (Node.js bot).
       3408 +  
       3409 +      Communicates with Node.js mineflayer bot via stdio.
       3410 +      """
       3411 +  
       3412 +      def __init__(self):
       3413 +          """Initialize Minecraft adapter."""
       3414 +          super().__init__()
       3415 +          self.bot_process = None
       3416 +          self.state = {}
       3417 +  
       3418 +      async def connect(
       3419 +          self,
       3420 +          host: str = "localhost",
       3421 +          port: int = 25565,
       3422 +          username: str = "WaifuBot",
       3423 +          version: str = "1.20.1",
       3424 +          **kwargs
       3425 +      ):
       3426 +          """
       3427 +          Connect to Minecraft server.
       3428 +  
       3429 +          Args:
       3430 +              host: Server hostname
       3431 +              port: Server port
       3432 +              username: Bot username (offline mode) or Microsoft account
       3433 +              version: Minecraft version
       3434 +          """
       3435 +          logger.info(f"Connecting to Minecraft server {host}:{port} as 
            + {username}")
       3436 +  
       3437 +          # Start mineflayer bot (Node.js subprocess)
       3438 +          bot_script = "backend/games/minecraft_bot.js"
       3439 +  
       3440 +          config = {
       3441 +              "host": host,
       3442 +              "port": port,
       3443 +              "username": username,
       3444 +              "version": version
       3445 +          }
       3446 +  
       3447 +          self.bot_process = subprocess.Popen(
       3448 +              ["node", bot_script, json.dumps(config)],
       3449 +              stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
       3450 +              stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
       3451 +              stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
       3452 +              text=True,
       3453 +              bufsize=1
       3454 +          )
       3455 +  
       3456 +          # Start reading output
       3457 +          asyncio.create_task(self._read_bot_output())
       3458 +  
       3459 +          self.connected = True
       3460 +          logger.info("✅ Minecraft bot started")
       3461 +  
       3462 +      async def disconnect(self):
       3463 +          """Disconnect from Minecraft server."""
       3464 +          if self.bot_process:
       3465 +              await self._send_command({"action": "disconnect"})
       3466 +              self.bot_process.wait(timeout=5)
       3467 +              self.bot_process = None
       3468 +              self.connected = False
       3469 +              logger.info("Minecraft bot disconnected")
       3470 +  
       3471 +      async def send_chat(self, message: str):
       3472 +          """
       3473 +          Send chat message in Minecraft.
       3474 +  
       3475 +          Args:
       3476 +              message: Chat message
       3477 +          """
       3478 +          await self._send_command({
       3479 +              "action": "chat",
       3480 +              "message": message
       3481 +          })
       3482 +  
       3483 +      async def get_state(self) -> Dict:
       3484 +          """
       3485 +          Get current bot state in Minecraft.
       3486 +  
       3487 +          Returns:
       3488 +              dict: {
       3489 +                  "position": {"x": float, "y": float, "z": float},
       3490 +                  "health": float,
       3491 +                  "food": float,
       3492 +                  "inventory": List[dict],
       3493 +                  "nearby_players": List[str]
       3494 +              }
       3495 +          """
       3496 +          return self.state
       3497 +  
       3498 +      async def execute_action(self, action: str, params: Dict = None):
       3499 +          """
       3500 +          Execute Minecraft action.
       3501 +  
       3502 +          Args:
       3503 +              action: Action name (goto, mine, place_block, attack, etc.)
       3504 +              params: Action parameters
       3505 +  
       3506 +          Example:
       3507 +              await adapter.execute_action("goto", {"x": 100, "y": 64, "z": 
            + 200})
       3508 +              await adapter.execute_action("mine", {"block_type": 
            + "diamond_ore"})
       3509 +          """
       3510 +          await self._send_command({
       3511 +              "action": action,
       3512 +              "params": params or {}
       3513 +          })
       3514 +  
       3515 +      async def _send_command(self, command: Dict):
       3516 +          """
       3517 +          Send command to mineflayer bot.
       3518 +  
       3519 +          Args:
       3520 +              command: Command dict
       3521 +          """
       3522 +          if self.bot_process and self.bot_process.stdin:
       3523 +              command_json = json.dumps(command) + "\n"
       3524 +              self.bot_process.stdin.write(command_json)
       3525 +              self.bot_process.stdin.flush()
       3526 +  
       3527 +      async def _read_bot_output(self):
       3528 +          """Read and process output from mineflayer bot."""
       3529 +          while self.bot_process and self.bot_process.stdout:
       3530 +              line = await asyncio.get_event_loop().run_in_executor(
       3531 +                  None,
       3532 +                  self.bot_process.stdout.readline
       3533 +              )
       3534 +  
       3535 +              if not line:
       3536 +                  break
       3537 +  
       3538 +              try:
       3539 +                  data = json.loads(line)
       3540 +                  event_type = data.get("event")
       3541 +  
       3542 +                  # Update state
       3543 +                  if "state" in data:
       3544 +                      self.state.update(data["state"])
       3545 +  
       3546 +                  # Emit events
       3547 +                  if event_type:
       3548 +                      await self.emit(event_type, data.get("data"))
       3549 +  
       3550 +              except json.JSONDecodeError:
       3551 +                  logger.warning(f"Invalid JSON from bot: {line}")
       3552 +              except Exception as e:
       3553 +                  logger.error(f"Error processing bot output: {e}")
       3554 +  
       3555 +  
       3556 +  # backend/games/minecraft_controller.py
       3557 +  from backend.games.minecraft_adapter import MinecraftAdapter
       3558 +  from backend.llm.registry import get_llm_adapter
       3559 +  import logging
       3560 +  
       3561 +  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
       3562 +  
       3563 +  class MinecraftController:
       3564 +      """
       3565 +      High-level controller for Minecraft AI.
       3566 +  
       3567 +      Connects game events to LLM decision-making.
       3568 +      """
       3569 +  
       3570 +      def __init__(self, adapter: MinecraftAdapter):
       3571 +          """
       3572 +          Initialize controller.
       3573 +  
       3574 +          Args:
       3575 +              adapter: MinecraftAdapter instance
       3576 +          """
       3577 +          self.adapter = adapter
       3578 +          self.llm = None
       3579 +  
       3580 +          # Register event handlers
       3581 +          self.adapter.on("chat", self.on_chat)
       3582 +          self.adapter.on("player_join", self.on_player_join)
       3583 +          self.adapter.on("damage", self.on_damage)
       3584 +  
       3585 +      async def initialize(self):
       3586 +          """Initialize LLM and other components."""
       3587 +          from backend.server import get_llm
       3588 +          self.llm = get_llm()
       3589 +          logger.info("Minecraft controller initialized")
       3590 +  
       3591 +      async def on_chat(self, data: Dict):
       3592 +          """
       3593 +          Handle chat messages in Minecraft.
       3594 +  
       3595 +          Args:
       3596 +              data: {"username": str, "message": str}
       3597 +          """
       3598 +          username = data["username"]
       3599 +          message = data["message"]
       3600 +  
       3601 +          logger.info(f"[Minecraft Chat] {username}: {message}")
       3602 +  
       3603 +          # Check if message mentions bot
       3604 +          if "waifu" in message.lower() or "bot" in message.lower():
       3605 +              response = await self.generate_response(username, message)
       3606 +              await self.adapter.send_chat(response)
       3607 +  
       3608 +      async def on_player_join(self, data: Dict):
       3609 +          """
       3610 +          Handle player join event.
       3611 +  
       3612 +          Args:
       3613 +              data: {"username": str}
       3614 +          """
       3615 +          username = data["username"]
       3616 +          logger.info(f"[Minecraft] Player joined: {username}")
       3617 +  
       3618 +          # Greet new player
       3619 +          await self.adapter.send_chat(f"Welcome {username}!")
       3620 +  
       3621 +      async def on_damage(self, data: Dict):
       3622 +          """
       3623 +          Handle damage event.
       3624 +  
       3625 +          Args:
       3626 +              data: {"damage": float, "source": str}
       3627 +          """
       3628 +          damage = data["damage"]
       3629 +          source = data.get("source", "unknown")
       3630 +  
       3631 +          logger.info(f"[Minecraft] Took {damage} damage from {source}")
       3632 +  
       3633 +          # React to damage
       3634 +          await self.adapter.send_chat(f"Ouch! {source} hurt me!")
       3635 +  
       3636 +      async def generate_response(self, username: str, message: str) -> str:
       3637 +          """
       3638 +          Generate AI response to chat message.
       3639 +  
       3640 +          Args:
       3641 +              username: Player who sent message
       3642 +              message: Chat message
       3643 +  
       3644 +          Returns:
       3645 +              AI response string
       3646 +          """
       3647 +          # Build context from game state
       3648 +          state = await self.adapter.get_state()
       3649 +          context = f"You are playing Minecraft. Position: 
            + {state.get('position')}, Health: {state.get('health')}/20"
       3650 +  
       3651 +          system_prompt = f"""You are an AI playing Minecraft with friends.
       3652 +  Be friendly, helpful, and respond naturally to chat messages.
       3653 +  Keep responses short (under 100 chars for Minecraft chat).
       3654 +  
       3655 +  Current game context: {context}"""
       3656 +  
       3657 +          messages = [
       3658 +              {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
       3659 +              {"role": "user", "content": f"{username} said: {message}"}
       3660 +          ]
       3661 +  
       3662 +          response = await self.llm.chat(messages=messages, max_tokens=50)
       3663 +  
       3664 +          # Clean response
       3665 +          response = response.replace("\n", " ").strip()
       3666 +          if len(response) > 100:
       3667 +              response = response[:97] + "..."
       3668 +  
       3669 +          return response
       3670 +  
       3671 +      async def execute_task(self, task: str):
       3672 +          """
       3673 +          Execute high-level task using LLM planning.
       3674 +  
       3675 +          Args:
       3676 +              task: Natural language task (e.g., "mine 10 diamonds")
       3677 +          """
       3678 +          logger.info(f"Executing task: {task}")
       3679 +  
       3680 +          # Ask LLM to break down task into steps
       3681 +          system_prompt = """You are an AI planning Minecraft actions.
       3682 +  Break down the user's task into specific actions.
       3683 +  Available actions: goto, mine, place_block, craft, attack, chat
       3684 +  
       3685 +  Respond with JSON array of actions:
       3686 +  [{"action": "goto", "params": {"x": 100, "y": 64, "z": 200}}, ...]"""
       3687 +  
       3688 +          messages = [
       3689 +              {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
       3690 +              {"role": "user", "content": f"Task: {task}"}
       3691 +          ]
       3692 +  
       3693 +          plan_json = await self.llm.chat(messages=messages, max_tokens=300)
       3694 +  
       3695 +          try:
       3696 +              plan = json.loads(plan_json)
       3697 +  
       3698 +              for step in plan:
       3699 +                  action = step["action"]
       3700 +                  params = step.get("params", {})
       3701 +  
       3702 +                  logger.info(f"Executing step: {action} with {params}")
       3703 +                  await self.adapter.execute_action(action, params)
       3704 +  
       3705 +                  # Wait between actions
       3706 +                  await asyncio.sleep(1)
       3707 +  
       3708 +          except json.JSONDecodeError:
       3709 +              logger.error(f"Failed to parse LLM plan: {plan_json}")
       3710 +  ```
       3711 +  
       3712 +  ```javascript
       3713 +  // backend/games/minecraft_bot.js
       3714 +  /**
       3715 +   * Mineflayer bot for Minecraft integration.
       3716 +   *
       3717 +   * Communicates with Python backend via stdin/stdout JSON.
       3718 +   * Uses Baritone for pathfinding.
       3719 +   */
       3720 +  
       3721 +  const mineflayer = require('mineflayer');
       3722 +  const { pathfinder, Movements, goals } = require('mineflayer-pathfinder');
       3723 +  
       3724 +  // Get config from command line args
       3725 +  const config = JSON.parse(process.argv[2]);
       3726 +  
       3727 +  // Create bot
       3728 +  const bot = mineflayer.createBot({
       3729 +      host: config.host,
       3730 +      port: config.port,
       3731 +      username: config.username,
       3732 +      version: config.version
       3733 +  });
       3734 +  
       3735 +  // Load pathfinder plugin
       3736 +  bot.loadPlugin(pathfinder);
       3737 +  
       3738 +  // Send event to Python
       3739 +  function sendEvent(event, data, state = null) {
       3740 +      const message = {
       3741 +          event: event,
       3742 +          data: data,
       3743 +          state: state || getState()
       3744 +      };
       3745 +      console.log(JSON.stringify(message));
       3746 +  }
       3747 +  
       3748 +  // Get current bot state
       3749 +  function getState() {
       3750 +      if (!bot.entity) return {};
       3751 +  
       3752 +      return {
       3753 +          position: bot.entity.position,
       3754 +          health: bot.health,
       3755 +          food: bot.food,
       3756 +          inventory: bot.inventory.items().map(item => ({
       3757 +              name: item.name,
       3758 +              count: item.count
       3759 +          })),
       3760 +          nearby_players: Object.keys(bot.players).filter(name => name !== 
            + bot.username)
       3761 +      };
       3762 +  }
       3763 +  
       3764 +  // Event handlers
       3765 +  bot.on('spawn', () => {
       3766 +      sendEvent('spawn', { message: 'Bot spawned in world' });
       3767 +  });
       3768 +  
       3769 +  bot.on('chat', (username, message) => {
       3770 +      if (username === bot.username) return;
       3771 +      sendEvent('chat', { username, message });
       3772 +  });
       3773 +  
       3774 +  bot.on('playerJoined', (player) => {
       3775 +      sendEvent('player_join', { username: player.username });
       3776 +  });
       3777 +  
       3778 +  bot.on('health', () => {
       3779 +      sendEvent('health_change', { health: bot.health, food: bot.food });
       3780 +  });
       3781 +  
       3782 +  bot.on('death', () => {
       3783 +      sendEvent('death', { message: 'Bot died' });
       3784 +  });
       3785 +  
       3786 +  bot.on('error', (err) => {
       3787 +      sendEvent('error', { error: err.message });
       3788 +  });
       3789 +  
       3790 +  // Command handler from Python
       3791 +  process.stdin.on('data', async (data) => {
       3792 +      try {
       3793 +          const command = JSON.parse(data.toString());
       3794 +          const { action, params = {} } = command;
       3795 +  
       3796 +          switch (action) {
       3797 +              case 'chat':
       3798 +                  bot.chat(params.message || command.message);
       3799 +                  break;
       3800 +  
       3801 +              case 'goto':
       3802 +                  // Use pathfinder to navigate
       3803 +                  const { x, y, z } = params;
       3804 +                  const goal = new goals.GoalBlock(x, y, z);
       3805 +                  const movements = new Movements(bot);
       3806 +                  bot.pathfinder.setMovements(movements);
       3807 +                  await bot.pathfinder.goto(goal);
       3808 +                  sendEvent('arrived', { position: { x, y, z } });
       3809 +                  break;
       3810 +  
       3811 +              case 'mine':
       3812 +                  // Find and mine block
       3813 +                  const blockType = params.block_type;
       3814 +                  const block = bot.findBlock({
       3815 +                      matching: (b) => b.name === blockType,
       3816 +                      maxDistance: 64
       3817 +                  });
       3818 +  
       3819 +                  if (block) {
       3820 +                      await bot.pathfinder.goto(new 
            + goals.GoalNear(block.position.x, block.position.y, block.position.z, 1));
       3821 +                      await bot.dig(block);
       3822 +                      sendEvent('mined', { block: blockType, position: 
            + block.position });
       3823 +                  } else {
       3824 +                      sendEvent('error', { message: `Block not found: 
            + ${blockType}` });
       3825 +                  }
       3826 +                  break;
       3827 +  
       3828 +              case 'place_block':
       3829 +                  // Place block
       3830 +                  const itemName = params.block_type;
       3831 +                  const item = bot.inventory.items().find(i => i.name === 
            + itemName);
       3832 +                  if (item) {
       3833 +                      await bot.equip(item, 'hand');
       3834 +                      const referenceBlock = 
            + bot.blockAt(bot.entity.position.offset(0, -1, 0));
       3835 +                      await bot.placeBlock(referenceBlock, new Vec3(0, 1, 
            + 0));
       3836 +                      sendEvent('placed', { block: itemName });
       3837 +                  } else {
       3838 +                      sendEvent('error', { message: `Item not in inventory: 
            + ${itemName}` });
       3839 +                  }
       3840 +                  break;
       3841 +  
       3842 +              case 'disconnect':
       3843 +                  bot.quit();
       3844 +                  process.exit(0);
       3845 +                  break;
       3846 +  
       3847 +              default:
       3848 +                  sendEvent('error', { message: `Unknown action: ${action}` 
            + });
       3849 +          }
       3850 +  
       3851 +      } catch (err) {
       3852 +          sendEvent('error', { error: err.message });
       3853 +      }
       3854 +  });
       3855 +  
       3856 +  // Periodic state updates
       3857 +  setInterval(() => {
       3858 +      sendEvent('state_update', {}, getState());
       3859 +  }, 5000); // Every 5 seconds
       3860 +  ```

       3937 +  - **Why Not:** Requires game developer cooperation
       3938 +  - **Use Case:** Future feature for custom game integration
       3939 +  
       3940 +  **4. Screen OCR + Mouse/Keyboard Control**
       3941 +  - **Approach:** Watch screen, control mouse/keyboard (like human player)
       3942 +  - **Why Not:** Very slow, unreliable, game-agnostic but low quality
       3943 +  - **Use Case:** Fallback for unsupported games
       3944 +  
       3945 +  **5. No Game Integration (Current)**
       3946 +  - **Approach:** AI is only a chat companion, doesn't play games
       3947 +  - **Why Not:** Misses major use case (co-op gaming, streaming)
       3948 +  - **Use Case:** Privacy-focused or non-gaming users
       3949 +

       3957 +  - **Mineflayer:** Mature, 6k+ GitHub stars, excellent docs
       3958 +  - **Content Potential:** Building, mining, PvP create entertaining moments
       3959 +  - **Cross-Platform:** Works on Java Edition servers

       3963 +  - **Plugins:** Pathfinder, PVP, auto-eat, many community plugins

       3980 +  
       3981 +  ## 9. Audio Emotion Recognition from Speech (SenseVoice, wav2vec2)
       3982 +  
       3983 +  ### Overview
       3984 +  Analyze emotional content from the user's voice (not just text) using 
            + SenseVoice or wav2vec2, providing the AI with richer emotional context. This
            +  detects emotions like anger, joy, sadness from speech prosody, pitch, and 
            + tone—even if text is neutral.
       3985 +  
       3986 +  ### What It Is and What It Does
       3987 +  Speech emotion recognition (SER) analyzes acoustic features of voice to 
            + detect emotional state:
       3988 +  
       3989 +  **What It Detects:**
       3990 +  - **7 Emotions:** Neutral, happy, sad, angry, fearful, disgusted, surprised
       3991 +  - **Prosody:** Speaking rhythm, stress patterns, intonation
       3992 +  - **Pitch:** Voice frequency (high pitch → excitement, low → sadness)
       3993 +  - **Energy:** Volume, intensity (loud → anger, soft → calm)
       3994 +  - **Tempo:** Speech rate (fast → anxiety, slow → calm)
       3995 +  
       3996 +  **Why Text Alone Isn't Enough:**
       3997 +  - Text: "I'm fine" → Appears neutral
       3998 +  - Voice: "I'm *fine*" (sarcastic tone, high pitch) → Actually frustrated
       3999 +  - AI with SER: Detects frustration, responds empathetically
       4000 +  
       4001 +  **How It Works:**
       4002 +  1. User speaks (microphone or uploaded audio)
       4003 +  2. Audio sent to SER model (SenseVoice or wav2vec2)
       4004 +  3. Model outputs emotion probabilities
       4005 +  4. Combine with text-based sentiment (suggestion #2)
       4006 +  5. AI adjusts tone/response based on voice emotion
       4007 +  
       4008 +  Example:
       4009 +  - User: "I'm fine" (but voice is shaky, low energy)
       4010 +  - SER detects: Sadness (0.75), Neutral (0.15), Fear (0.10)
       4011 +  - AI: "You sound a bit down. Want to talk about it?"
       4012 +  
       4013 +  ### Code Example
       4014 +  
       4015 +  ```python
       4016 +  # backend/emotion/speech_emotion.py
       4017 +  import torch
       4018 +  import torchaudio
       4019 +  from transformers import AutoFeatureExtractor, 
            + AutoModelForAudioClassification
       4020 +  from typing import Dict, Optional
       4021 +  from pathlib import Path
       4022 +  import numpy as np
       4023 +  import logging
       4024 +  
       4025 +  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
       4026 +  
       4027 +  class SpeechEmotionRecognizer:
       4028 +      """
       4029 +      Speech emotion recognition using SenseVoice or wav2vec2.
       4030 +  
       4031 +      Analyzes audio to detect emotional state from voice characteristics.
       4032 +      """
       4033 +  
       4034 +      def __init__(
       4035 +          self,
       4036 +          model_name: str = "m-a-p/MERT-v1-330M-emotion",
       4037 +          device: str = "auto"
       4038 +      ):
       4039 +          """
       4040 +          Initialize speech emotion recognizer.
       4041 +  
       4042 +          Args:
       4043 +              model_name: HuggingFace model identifier
       4044 +                  Options:
       4045 +                  - "m-a-p/MERT-v1-330M-emotion" (music/speech emotion, 330M 
            + params)
       4046 +                  - 
            + "ehcalabres/wav2vec2-lg-xlsr-en-speech-emotion-recognition" (7 emotions)
       4047 +                  - "FunAudioLLM/SenseVoiceSmall" (multilingual, 
            + Chinese-focused)
       4048 +              device: "auto", "cuda", or "cpu"
       4049 +          """
       4050 +          self.model_name = model_name
       4051 +  
       4052 +          # Determine device
       4053 +          if device == "auto":
       4054 +              self.device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
       4055 +          else:
       4056 +              self.device = device
       4057 +  
       4058 +          logger.info(f"Loading speech emotion model: {model_name} (device: 
            + {self.device})")
       4059 +  
       4060 +          # Load feature extractor and model
       4061 +          self.feature_extractor = 
            + AutoFeatureExtractor.from_pretrained(model_name)
       4062 +          self.model = 
            + AutoModelForAudioClassification.from_pretrained(model_name)
       4063 +          self.model.to(self.device)
       4064 +          self.model.eval()
       4065 +  
       4066 +          # Emotion labels (depends on model)
       4067 +          self.emotion_labels = self._get_emotion_labels()
       4068 +  
       4069 +          logger.info(f"✅ Speech emotion model loaded 
            + ({len(self.emotion_labels)} emotions)")
       4070 +  
       4071 +      def _get_emotion_labels(self) -> list:
       4072 +          """Get emotion label list from model config."""
       4073 +          if hasattr(self.model.config, 'id2label'):
       4074 +              return [self.model.config.id2label[i] for i in 
            + range(len(self.model.config.id2label))]
       4075 +          else:
       4076 +              # Default emotions for wav2vec2 SER models
       4077 +              return ["neutral", "happy", "sad", "angry", "fearful", 
            + "disgust", "surprised"]
       4078 +  
       4079 +      def analyze_audio_file(self, audio_path: Path) -> Dict:
       4080 +          """
       4081 +          Analyze emotion from audio file.
       4082 +  
       4083 +          Args:
       4084 +              audio_path: Path to audio file (WAV, MP3, etc.)
       4085 +  
       4086 +          Returns:
       4087 +              dict: {
       4088 +                  "emotion": str,  # Primary emotion
       4089 +                  "confidence": float,  # Confidence score (0-1)
       4090 +                  "all_emotions": dict,  # All emotions with scores
       4091 +                  "model": str  # Model name
       4092 +              }
       4093 +          """
       4094 +          # Load audio
       4095 +          waveform, sample_rate = torchaudio.load(audio_path)
       4096 +  
       4097 +          return self.analyze_audio(waveform, sample_rate)
       4098 +  
       4099 +      def analyze_audio(self, waveform: torch.Tensor, sample_rate: int) -> 
            + Dict:
       4100 +          """
       4101 +          Analyze emotion from audio waveform.
       4102 +  
       4103 +          Args:
       4104 +              waveform: Audio tensor (shape: [channels, samples])
       4105 +              sample_rate: Sample rate (Hz)
       4106 +  
       4107 +          Returns:
       4108 +              Emotion analysis dict
       4109 +          """
       4110 +          # Convert stereo to mono if needed
       4111 +          if waveform.shape[0] > 1:
       4112 +              waveform = torch.mean(waveform, dim=0, keepdim=True)
       4113 +  
       4114 +          # Resample if needed (most models expect 16kHz)
       4115 +          target_sr = self.feature_extractor.sampling_rate
       4116 +          if sample_rate != target_sr:
       4117 +              resampler = torchaudio.transforms.Resample(sample_rate, 
            + target_sr)
       4118 +              waveform = resampler(waveform)
       4119 +              sample_rate = target_sr
       4120 +  
       4121 +          # Convert to numpy for feature extractor
       4122 +          audio_array = waveform.squeeze().numpy()
       4123 +  
       4124 +          # Extract features
       4125 +          inputs = self.feature_extractor(
       4126 +              audio_array,
       4127 +              sampling_rate=sample_rate,
       4128 +              return_tensors="pt",
       4129 +              padding=True
       4130 +          )
       4131 +  
       4132 +          # Move to device
       4133 +          inputs = {k: v.to(self.device) for k, v in inputs.items()}
       4134 +  
       4135 +          # Run inference
       4136 +          with torch.no_grad():
       4137 +              outputs = self.model(**inputs)
       4138 +              logits = outputs.logits
       4139 +  
       4140 +          # Get probabilities
       4141 +          probs = torch.nn.functional.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
       4142 +          probs = probs.cpu().numpy()[0]
       4143 +  
       4144 +          # Build results
       4145 +          all_emotions = {
       4146 +              self.emotion_labels[i]: float(probs[i])
       4147 +              for i in range(len(probs))
       4148 +          }
       4149 +  
       4150 +          # Get primary emotion
       4151 +          primary_idx = np.argmax(probs)
       4152 +          primary_emotion = self.emotion_labels[primary_idx]
       4153 +          confidence = float(probs[primary_idx])
       4154 +  
       4155 +          return {
       4156 +              "emotion": primary_emotion,
       4157 +              "confidence": round(confidence, 3),
       4158 +              "all_emotions": {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in 
            + all_emotions.items()},
       4159 +              "model": self.model_name
       4160 +          }
       4161 +  
       4162 +      def analyze_audio_chunk(self, audio_bytes: bytes, sample_rate: int = 
            + 16000) -> Dict:
       4163 +          """
       4164 +          Analyze emotion from raw audio bytes (for real-time).
       4165 +  
       4166 +          Args:
       4167 +              audio_bytes: Raw audio data (int16 PCM)
       4168 +              sample_rate: Sample rate (Hz)
       4169 +  
       4170 +          Returns:
       4171 +              Emotion analysis dict
       4172 +          """
       4173 +          # Convert bytes to tensor
       4174 +          audio_array = np.frombuffer(audio_bytes, dtype=np.int16)
       4175 +          audio_array = audio_array.astype(np.float32) / 32768.0  # Normalize
            +  to [-1, 1]
       4176 +  
       4177 +          waveform = torch.from_numpy(audio_array).unsqueeze(0)  # Add 
            + channel dimension
       4178 +  
       4179 +          return self.analyze_audio(waveform, sample_rate)
       4180 +  
       4181 +  
       4182 +  # Integration in backend/server.py
       4183 +  from backend.emotion.speech_emotion import SpeechEmotionRecognizer
       4184 +  from backend.emotion.advanced_sentiment import AdvancedSentimentAnalyzer
       4185 +  from fastapi import File, UploadFile
       4186 +  
       4187 +  speech_emotion = None
       4188 +  
       4189 +  def get_speech_emotion():
       4190 +      """Lazy-load speech emotion recognizer."""
       4191 +      global speech_emotion
       4192 +      if speech_emotion is None:
       4193 +          speech_emotion = SpeechEmotionRecognizer()
       4194 +      return speech_emotion
       4195 +  
       4196 +  @app.post("/api/emotion/analyze-speech")
       4197 +  async def analyze_speech_emotion(file: UploadFile = File(...)):
       4198 +      """
       4199 +      Analyze emotion from uploaded audio file.
       4200 +  
       4201 +      Args:

       4203 +  
       4204 +      Returns:

       4210 +

       4213 +

       4217 +  
       4218 +      # Clean up temp file
       4219 +      temp_path.unlink()
       4220 +  
       4221 +      return {
       4222 +          "ok": True,
       4223 +          "speech_emotion": result["emotion"],
       4224 +          "confidence": result["confidence"],
       4225 +          "all_emotions": result["all_emotions"]
       4226 +      }
       4227 +  
       4228 +  @app.post("/api/chat/with-voice")
       4229 +  async def chat_with_voice(
       4230 +      text: str,
       4231 +      file: UploadFile = File(...),
       4232 +      session_id: int = 1
       4233 +  ):
       4234 +      """
       4235 +      Chat with both text and voice emotion analysis.
       4236 +  
       4237 +      Args:
       4238 +          text: Transcribed text
       4239 +          file: Audio file of user's speech
       4240 +          session_id: Session ID
       4241 +  
       4242 +      Returns:
       4243 +          AI response with multimodal emotion understanding
       4244 +      """
       4245 +      # Analyze text emotion (from suggestion #2)
       4246 +      text_analyzer = get_sentiment_analyzer()
       4247 +      text_emotion = text_analyzer.analyze(text)
       4248 +  
       4249 +      # Analyze speech emotion
       4250 +      temp_path = Path(f"backend/storage/temp/voice_{session_id}.wav")
       4251 +      temp_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
       4252 +  
       4253 +      with open(temp_path, "wb") as f:
       4254 +          f.write(await file.read())
       4255 +  
       4256 +      ser = get_speech_emotion()
       4257 +      speech_emotion = ser.analyze_audio_file(temp_path)
       4258 +      temp_path.unlink()
       4259 +  
       4260 +      # Combine emotions (prioritize speech if confident)
       4261 +      if speech_emotion["confidence"] > 0.6:
       4262 +          final_emotion = speech_emotion["emotion"]
       4263 +          emotion_source = "speech"
       4264 +      else:
       4265 +          final_emotion = text_emotion["emotion"]
       4266 +          emotion_source = "text"
       4267 +  
       4268 +      # Build context for LLM
       4269 +      emotion_context = f"""
       4270 +  [User Emotion Analysis]
       4271 +  - Text emotion: {text_emotion['emotion']} (confidence: 
            + {text_emotion['intensity']})
       4272 +  - Speech emotion: {speech_emotion['emotion']} (confidence: 
            + {speech_emotion['confidence']})
       4273 +  - Final emotion: {final_emotion} (source: {emotion_source})
       4274 +  
       4275 +  The user's voice reveals their emotional state. Respond empathetically.
       4276 +  """
       4277 +  
       4278 +      # Get character and build messages
       4279 +      char = load_character(1)
       4280 +      messages = load_history(session_id, max_history=10)
       4281 +  
       4282 +      # Inject emotion context into system prompt
       4283 +      enhanced_system_prompt = char['system_prompt'] + "\n\n" + 
            + emotion_context
       4284 +      messages[0] = {"role": "system", "content": enhanced_system_prompt}
       4285 +  
       4286 +      messages.append({"role": "user", "content": text})
       4287 +  
       4288 +      # Get LLM response
       4289 +      llm = get_llm()
       4290 +      reply = await llm.chat(messages, model=cfg["llm"]["model"], ...)
       4291 +  
       4292 +      # Save messages
       4293 +      save_message(session_id, "user", text, metadata={
       4294 +          "text_emotion": text_emotion["emotion"],
       4295 +          "speech_emotion": speech_emotion["emotion"]
       4296 +      })
       4297 +      save_message(session_id, "assistant", reply)
       4298 +  
       4299 +      return {
       4300 +          "ok": True,
       4301 +          "reply": reply,
       4302 +          "text_emotion": text_emotion,
       4303 +          "speech_emotion": speech_emotion,
       4304 +          "final_emotion": final_emotion
       4305 +      }
       4306 +  ```

       4332 +  
       4333 +  ### Pros
       4334 +  ✅ **Multimodal Emotion:** Detects emotions text misses (sarcasm, 
            + suppressed feelings)
       4335 +  ✅ **Empathy:** AI can respond to user's true emotional state
       4336 +  ✅ **Richer Interaction:** Voice reveals more than words
       4337 +  ✅ **Cross-Lingual:** Works even if text language differs
       4338 +  ✅ **Real-Time Capable:** Can analyze speech chunks in real-time
       4339 +  ✅ **Open Source:** Multiple free models available
       4340 +  ✅ **Complements Text:** Combines with suggestion #2 for best accuracy
       4341 +  
       4342 +  ### Cons
       4343 +  ❌ **Model Size:** 300-500MB model download
       4344 +  ❌ **Accuracy Variance:** Quality depends on recording (noise, mic quality)
       4345 +  ❌ **Latency:** Adds 100-300ms processing time
       4346 +  ❌ **Privacy:** Requires audio upload (sensitive data)
       4347 +  ❌ **Language Support:** Most models English-only or English-best
       4348 +  ❌ **False Positives:** Background noise can affect results
       4349 +  
       4350 +  ### Alternatives Considered
       4351 +  
       4352 +  **1. OpenAI Whisper with Emotion Fine-Tuning**
       4353 +  - **Approach:** Fine-tune Whisper ASR model for emotion classification
       4354 +  - **Why Not:** Whisper not designed for emotion, would need custom training
       4355 +  - **Use Case:** If we're already using Whisper for ASR (suggestion #14)
       4356 +  
       4357 +  **2. Hume AI API (Commercial)**
       4358 +  - **Approach:** Use Hume AI's emotion API ($0.005-0.02 per minute)
       4359 +  - **Why Not:** Costs add up, cloud dependency, privacy concerns
       4360 +  - **Use Case:** If local inference unacceptable
       4361 +  
       4362 +  **3. pyAudioAnalysis (Traditional ML)**
       4363 +  - **Approach:** Extract acoustic features (MFCCs), train SVM/Random Forest
       4364 +  - **Why Not:** Lower accuracy than deep learning, need labeled dataset
       4365 +  - **Use Case:** If model size is critical constraint
       4366 +  
       4367 +  **4. Browser Web Audio API Analysis**
       4368 +  - **Approach:** Analyze pitch, energy in browser JavaScript
       4369 +  - **Why Not:** Can't detect emotions accurately, only basic features
       4370 +  - **Use Case:** Real-time pitch visualization (not emotion)
       4371 +  
       4372 +  **5. Text Emotion Only (Suggestion #2)**
       4373 +  - **Approach:** Only analyze text, ignore speech prosody
       4374 +  - **Why Not:** Misses important emotional cues (tone, sarcasm)
       4375 +  - **Use Case:** If voice input not used
       4376 +  
       4377 +  ### Reasoning for wav2vec2-based SER
       4378 +  
       4379 +  **Why Speech Emotion:** Human communication is 38% vocal, 55% body 
            + language, only 7% words (Mehrabian's research). Text-only emotion misses 
            + most emotional information. For empathetic AI, voice analysis is essential.
       4380 +  
       4381 +  **Why wav2vec2:**
       4382 +  - **State-of-the-Art:** Transformer-based, pre-trained on 60k hours of 
            + speech
       4383 +  - **Open Source:** MIT/Apache licenses
       4384 +  - **Multiple Options:** Many fine-tuned models on HuggingFace
       4385 +  - **Proven:** Used in research, production emotion analysis
       4386 +  
       4387 +  **Why Not Commercial APIs:**
       4388 +  - **Privacy:** Voice is biometric data, shouldn't leave device
       4389 +  - **Cost:** $0.005-0.02 per minute adds up
       4390 +  - **Latency:** API adds 200-500ms
       4391 +  - **Offline:** Local works without internet
       4392 +  
       4393 +  **Multimodal Fusion Strategy:**
       4394 +  - If speech confident (>0.6): Use speech emotion
       4395 +  - If speech uncertain: Use text emotion as fallback
       4396 +  - Log both for debugging and improvement
       4397 +

       4406 +  
       4407 +  ## 10. WebRTC Streaming for Multi-User Sessions (Peer-to-Peer Avatar 
            + Streaming)
       4408 +  
       4409 +  ### Overview
       4410 +  Implement WebRTC-based peer-to-peer streaming to enable multiple users to 
            + see and interact with the same 3D avatar in real-time. This creates shared 
            + experiences where users can watch AI interactions together, similar to 
            + Twitch streams but with lower latency.
       4411 +  
       4412 +  ### What It Is and What It Does
       4413 +  WebRTC (Web Real-Time Communication) enables peer-to-peer audio/video 
            + streaming in browsers without plugins:
       4414 +  
       4415 +  **Capabilities:**
       4416 +  - **Multi-User Viewing:** Multiple users see same 3D avatar in sync
       4417 +  - **Low Latency:** <100ms delay (vs 2-5s for Twitch)
       4418 +  - **Peer-to-Peer:** Direct browser connections, no central server (after 
            + signaling)
       4419 +  - **Interactive:** All users can chat with AI, see each other's 
            + interactions
       4420 +  - **Screen Sharing:** Host can share avatar view with viewers
       4421 +  - **Synchronization:** Avatar animations, TTS audio synced across all 
            + viewers
       4422 +  
       4423 +  **Use Cases:**
       4424 +  - **Watch Parties:** Friends watch AI together
       4425 +  - **Streaming:** Stream AI to viewers without Twitch/YouTube
       4426 +  - **Collaboration:** Multiple users interact with same AI instance
       4427 +  - **Demos:** Show AI to others in real-time
       4428 +  
       4429 +  **Architecture:**
       4430 +  ```
       4431 +  Host Browser (has AI connection)
       4432 +    ↓ WebRTC
       4433 +    → Viewer 1 Browser
       4434 +    → Viewer 2 Browser
       4435 +    → Viewer 3 Browser
       4436 +    ...
       4437 +  ```
       4438 +  
       4439 +  Host's browser captures 3D canvas + audio, streams to viewers via WebRTC.
       4440 +  
       4441 +  ### Code Example
       4442 +  
       4443 +  ```python
       4444 +  # backend/streaming/webrtc_signaling.py
       4445 +  from fastapi import WebSocket, WebSocketDisconnect
       4446 +  from typing import Dict, Set
       4447 +  import json
       4448 +  import logging
       4449 +  
       4450 +  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
       4451 +  
       4452 +  class WebRTCSignalingServer:
       4453 +      """
       4454 +      WebRTC signaling server for peer-to-peer avatar streaming.
       4455 +  
       4456 +      Facilitates peer connection setup (SDP exchange, ICE candidates).
       4457 +      Actual media streams peer-to-peer after connection established.
       4458 +      """
       4459 +  
       4460 +      def __init__(self):
       4461 +          """Initialize signaling server."""
       4462 +          self.rooms: Dict[str, Set[WebSocket]] = {}  # room_id -> set of 
            + websockets
       4463 +          self.hosts: Dict[str, WebSocket] = {}  # room_id -> host websocket
       4464 +  
       4465 +      async def handle_websocket(self, websocket: WebSocket, room_id: str, 
            + is_host: bool = False):
       4466 +          """
       4467 +          Handle WebSocket connection for WebRTC signaling.
       4468 +  
       4469 +          Args:
       4470 +              websocket: FastAPI WebSocket
       4471 +              room_id: Room identifier
       4472 +              is_host: True if this is the streaming host
       4473 +          """
       4474 +          await websocket.accept()
       4475 +  
       4476 +          # Create room if doesn't exist
       4477 +          if room_id not in self.rooms:
       4478 +              self.rooms[room_id] = set()
       4479 +  
       4480 +          # Add to room
       4481 +          self.rooms[room_id].add(websocket)
       4482 +  
       4483 +          if is_host:
       4484 +              self.hosts[room_id] = websocket
       4485 +              logger.info(f"Host joined room: {room_id}")
       4486 +          else:
       4487 +              logger.info(f"Viewer joined room: {room_id} (total: 
            + {len(self.rooms[room_id])})")
       4488 +  
       4489 +          try:
       4490 +              while True:
       4491 +                  # Receive message from client
       4492 +                  data = await websocket.receive_text()
       4493 +                  message = json.loads(data)
       4494 +  
       4495 +                  # Forward signaling messages to appropriate peer
       4496 +                  await self.route_message(websocket, room_id, message)
       4497 +  
       4498 +          except WebSocketDisconnect:
       4499 +              # Remove from room
       4500 +              self.rooms[room_id].remove(websocket)
       4501 +  
       4502 +              if is_host and room_id in self.hosts:
       4503 +                  del self.hosts[room_id]
       4504 +                  # Notify all viewers that host left
       4505 +                  await self.broadcast_to_room(room_id, {
       4506 +                      "type": "host_left",
       4507 +                      "message": "Host disconnected"
       4508 +                  })
       4509 +                  logger.info(f"Host left room: {room_id}")
       4510 +              else:
       4511 +                  logger.info(f"Viewer left room: {room_id}")
       4512 +  
       4513 +              # Clean up empty rooms
       4514 +              if not self.rooms[room_id]:
       4515 +                  del self.rooms[room_id]
       4516 +  
       4517 +      async def route_message(self, sender: WebSocket, room_id: str, message:
            +  dict):
       4518 +          """
       4519 +          Route signaling message to appropriate peer.
       4520 +  
       4521 +          Args:
       4522 +              sender: WebSocket that sent message
       4523 +              room_id: Room identifier
       4524 +              message: Signaling message (SDP offer/answer, ICE candidate)
       4525 +          """
       4526 +          msg_type = message.get("type")
       4527 +  
       4528 +          if msg_type == "offer":
       4529 +              # Viewer sends offer to host
       4530 +              if room_id in self.hosts:
       4531 +                  await self.hosts[room_id].send_text(json.dumps({
       4532 +                      "type": "offer",
       4533 +                      "sdp": message["sdp"],
       4534 +                      "viewer_id": id(sender)
       4535 +                  }))
       4536 +  
       4537 +          elif msg_type == "answer":
       4538 +              # Host sends answer back to viewer
       4539 +              viewer_id = message.get("viewer_id")
       4540 +              for ws in self.rooms[room_id]:
       4541 +                  if id(ws) == viewer_id:
       4542 +                      await ws.send_text(json.dumps({
       4543 +                          "type": "answer",
       4544 +                          "sdp": message["sdp"]
       4545 +                      }))
       4546 +                      break
       4547 +  
       4548 +          elif msg_type == "ice-candidate":
       4549 +              # Forward ICE candidates between peers
       4550 +              if sender == self.hosts.get(room_id):
       4551 +                  # Host → Viewer
       4552 +                  viewer_id = message.get("viewer_id")
       4553 +                  for ws in self.rooms[room_id]:
       4554 +                      if id(ws) == viewer_id:
       4555 +                          await ws.send_text(json.dumps({
       4556 +                              "type": "ice-candidate",
       4557 +                              "candidate": message["candidate"]
       4558 +                          }))
       4559 +                          break
       4560 +              else:
       4561 +                  # Viewer → Host
       4562 +                  if room_id in self.hosts:
       4563 +                      await self.hosts[room_id].send_text(json.dumps({
       4564 +                          "type": "ice-candidate",
       4565 +                          "candidate": message["candidate"],
       4566 +                          "viewer_id": id(sender)
       4567 +                      }))
       4568 +  
       4569 +      async def broadcast_to_room(self, room_id: str, message: dict):
       4570 +          """
       4571 +          Broadcast message to all peers in room.
       4572 +  
       4573 +          Args:
       4574 +              room_id: Room identifier
       4575 +              message: Message to broadcast
       4576 +          """
       4577 +          if room_id not in self.rooms:
       4578 +              return
       4579 +  
       4580 +          message_json = json.dumps(message)
       4581 +  
       4582 +          for ws in self.rooms[room_id]:
       4583 +              try:
       4584 +                  await ws.send_text(message_json)
       4585 +              except Exception as e:
       4586 +                  logger.error(f"Error broadcasting to peer: {e}")
       4587 +  
       4588 +  
       4589 +  # Integration in backend/server.py
       4590 +  from backend.streaming.webrtc_signaling import WebRTCSignalingServer
       4591 +  
       4592 +  webrtc_signaling = WebRTCSignalingServer()
       4593 +  
       4594 +  @app.websocket("/ws/webrtc/{room_id}/host")
       4595 +  async def webrtc_host(websocket: WebSocket, room_id: str):

       4635 +      constructor(roomId, signalingUrl =

       4637 +          this.signalingUrl = signalingUrl;

       4640 +          this.stream = null;
       4641 +      }
       4642 +  
       4643 +      async start(canvas) {

       4645 +          this.stream = canvas.captureStream(30); // 30 FPS
       4646 +

       4649 +  
       4650 +          this.signalingWs.onopen = () => {
       4651 +              console.log('WebRTC host connected to signaling server');
       4652 +          };
       4653 +  
       4654 +          this.signalingWs.onmessage = async (event) => {

       4661 +  
       4662 +      async handleSignalingMessage(message) {
       4663 +          const { type, viewer_id } = message;
       4664 +  
       4665 +          switch (type) {
       4666 +              case 'offer':
       4667 +                  // Viewer sent offer, create answer
       4668 +                  await this.handleOffer(message.sdp, viewer_id);
       4669 +                  break;
       4670 +  
       4671 +              case 'ice-candidate':
       4672 +                  // Viewer sent ICE candidate
       4673 +                  const pc = this.peerConnections.get(viewer_id);
       4674 +                  if (pc && message.candidate) {
       4675 +                      await pc.addIceCandidate(new 
            + RTCIceCandidate(message.candidate));
       4676 +                  }
       4677 +                  break;
       4678 +          }
       4679 +      }
       4680 +  
       4681 +      async handleOffer(sdp, viewerId) {
       4682 +          // Create peer connection for this viewer
       4683 +          const pc = new RTCPeerConnection({
       4684 +              iceServers: [
       4685 +                  { urls: 'stun:stun.l.google.com:19302' },
       4686 +                  { urls: 'stun:stun1.l.google.com:19302' }
       4687 +              ]
       4688 +          });
       4689 +  
       4690 +          this.peerConnections.set(viewerId, pc);
       4691 +  
       4692 +          // Add stream tracks
       4693 +          this.stream.getTracks().forEach(track => {
       4694 +              pc.addTrack(track, this.stream);
       4695 +          });
       4696 +  
       4697 +          // Handle ICE candidates
       4698 +          pc.onicecandidate = (event) => {
       4699 +              if (event.candidate) {
       4700 +                  this.signalingWs.send(JSON.stringify({
       4701 +                      type: 'ice-candidate',
       4702 +                      candidate: event.candidate,
       4703 +                      viewer_id: viewerId
       4704 +                  }));
       4705 +              }
       4706 +          };
       4707 +  
       4708 +          // Set remote description (offer from viewer)
       4709 +          await pc.setRemoteDescription(new RTCSessionDescription({ type: 
            + 'offer', sdp }));
       4710 +  
       4711 +          // Create answer
       4712 +          const answer = await pc.createAnswer();
       4713 +          await pc.setLocalDescription(answer);
       4714 +  
       4715 +          // Send answer to viewer
       4716 +          this.signalingWs.send(JSON.stringify({
       4717 +              type: 'answer',
       4718 +              sdp: answer.sdp,
       4719 +              viewer_id: viewerId
       4720 +          }));
       4721 +  
       4722 +          console.log(`Created peer connection for viewer ${viewerId}`);
       4723 +      }
       4724 +  
       4725 +      stop() {
       4726 +          // Close all peer connections
       4727 +          this.peerConnections.forEach(pc => pc.close());
       4728 +          this.peerConnections.clear();
       4729 +  
       4730 +          // Close signaling WebSocket
       4731 +          if (this.signalingWs) {
       4732 +              this.signalingWs.close();
       4733 +          }
       4734 +  
       4735 +          // Stop media stream
       4736 +          if (this.stream) {
       4737 +              this.stream.getTracks().forEach(track => track.stop());
       4738 +          }
       4739 +  
       4740 +          console.log('WebRTC host stopped');
       4741 +      }
       4742 +  }

       4800 +  
       4801 +          this.signalingWs.onmessage = async (event) => {
       4802 +              const message = JSON.parse(event.data);

       4931 +  ### Pros
       4932 +  ✅ **Low Latency:** <100ms (vs 2-5s for Twitch/YouTube)
       4933 +  ✅ **Peer-to-Peer:** No bandwidth cost for server (after signaling)
       4934 +  ✅ **Browser Native:** No plugins or external software
       4935 +  ✅ **Interactive:** Viewers can chat with AI in real-time
       4936 +  ✅ **Private Rooms:** Share URL only with friends
       4937 +  ✅ **Synchronized:** All viewers see same avatar state
       4938 +  ✅ **Scalable:** Each host can stream to 10-20 viewers
       4939 +  
       4940 +  ### Cons
       4941 +  ❌ **NAT Traversal:** Requires STUN/TURN servers for some networks
       4942 +  ❌ **Browser Only:** No native app support (use browser)
       4943 +  ❌ **Bandwidth:** Host uploads to each viewer (N viewers = N times 
            + bandwidth)
       4944 +  ❌ **Connection Limits:** Typical limit 10-20 viewers per host
       4945 +  ❌ **No Recording:** Unlike Twitch, no automatic VODs
       4946 +  ❌ **Complexity:** WebRTC setup more complex than HTTP streaming
       4947 +  
       4948 +  ### Alternatives Considered
       4949 +  
       4950 +  **1. Twitch/YouTube Streaming (OBS + Stream Key)**
       4951 +  - **Approach:** Use OBS to capture browser, stream to Twitch
       4952 +  - **Why Not:** 2-5s latency, requires OBS setup, less interactive
       4953 +  - **Use Case:** Public streaming to large audiences (100+)
       4954 +  
       4955 +  **2. HLS/DASH HTTP Streaming**
       4956 +  - **Approach:** Encode canvas to HLS, serve via HTTP
       4957 +  - **Why Not:** 5-10s latency, server bandwidth costs
       4958 +  - **Use Case:** VOD playback, not real-time
       4959 +  
       4960 +  **3. WebSocket Canvas Streaming**
       4961 +  - **Approach:** Send canvas frames via WebSocket
       4962 +  - **Why Not:** Inefficient (no video compression), high bandwidth
       4963 +  - **Use Case:** Simple demos, low framerate
       4964 +  
       4965 +  **4. Self-Hosted RTMP Server (nginx-rtmp)**
       4966 +  - **Approach:** Stream to self-hosted RTMP server, viewers watch via HLS
       4967 +  - **Why Not:** Complex setup, latency, server costs
       4968 +  - **Use Case:** If hosting for large audience
       4969 +  
       4970 +  **5. Discord Screen Share**
       4971 +  - **Approach:** Share browser tab via Discord screen share
       4972 +  - **Why Not:** Discord-specific, 720p limit, compressed
       4973 +  - **Use Case:** Quick demos to friends already on Discord
       4974 +  
       4975 +  ### Reasoning for WebRTC
       4976 +  
       4977 +  **Why Streaming:** Users want to share AI interactions with friends, create
            +  content, showcase character personalities. Neuro-sama's streams have 
            + millions of views—users want same capability.
       4978 +  
       4979 +  **Why WebRTC:**
       4980 +  - **Real-Time:** <100ms latency enables interactive experiences
       4981 +  - **Free:** No streaming service fees, no bandwidth costs (peer-to-peer)
       4982 +  - **Private:** No public platform, share URL only with friends
       4983 +  - **Browser Native:** Works immediately, no OBS/software setup
       4984 +  - **Flexible:** Works for 1-on-1 or small groups
       4985 +  
       4986 +  **Why Not Twitch:**
       4987 +  - Still recommend for large audiences (100+)
       4988 +  - WebRTC for small groups, Twitch for public
       4989 +  - Can do both simultaneously
       4990 +  
       4991 +  **STUN/TURN Setup:**
       4992 +  - Use free STUN servers (stun.l.google.com)
       4993 +  - For production: Self-host TURN server (coturn) or use service
       4994 +  - Most connections work with STUN only (~80%)
       4995 +
